reviews.text: Roguelike-soulslike games are surprisingly hard to come by considering the popularity of both genres. Loving what i'm playing so far from this has a very Dead Cells progression loot of seperating items into colored categories and meta progression using a merchant between levels - so far my biggest complaint might be i-frames on dodge rolls not starting as early as they do in other soulslikes and the 2 bosses i've faced so far are a little -too easy- (Bound Prisoner and Disgraced Chieftain). Popped into settings and turned on those sweet, sweet retro settings though! Love the aesthetics. Well worth the price so far!

I´m sorry but I cannot recommend this game. The runs are very short, the game is, in general, pretty easy. The amount of content is pretty small, theres little to do here. For a game that advertises itself as Souls-like the game is way too short. Still - pretty fun with what it has alredy. The graphics are actually alright

Here my gameplay (finished the game in this run): https://youtu.be/2s_0Yigu-ho A solid roguelite - lots of meta progression - interesting bosses with different mechanics and attack patterns Only downside is, that it is a bit short lived before it gets too repetitive to keep replay another run.

Really solid and absolutely worth the price tag. This is coming from a guy who thought he was tired of the souls like thing. Something about this drew me to it and Im glad it did. It's charming. It isnt groundbreaking in any way, but it does things right and does things well. Difficulty is there, but it's not insane. I made it to the 3rd boss my first session (I did die 7 times though before making it to him) Love the whole aesthetic and style overall. Very appealing and fun. Here is my video review: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LWDEI6t40D4

I have only put in 90 minutes but I am already able to tell you this game is perfect. The combat feels so nice, the visual effects to turn it into a ps1 aesthetic complete with texture warping is so delightful. Just a great mixture of dark souls and dead cells. Two games I can never get enough of. Absolutely excellent job gang, this is such a wonderful game.

勉强吧。攻击动作只有轻攻击和重攻击两种，没有冲刺翻滚攻击这些。打怪能掉对应怪身上装备的制作书，然后在商人那花钱解锁。有一点很重要，千万不要乱解锁，这样会污染装备池。服装我就解锁了一件邪教徒的服装，可以给武器上毒。因为装备池少，所以很容易捡到，同时还能捡到红色的盗贼服装，从尸体上摸金币的。清完关，换上后摸一遍再换回来。盾牌我一般用默认装备池的翻滚不耗精的绿色盾牌，不额外解锁。武器上，解锁设计图的绿色的狱卒剑伤害非常高，然后第一个BOSS掉的红色骷髅拳套也是YYDS，其他没有乱解锁，千万别乱解锁。升级根据你用狱卒剑还是骷髅拳套升绿色或红色。装备缺很多，不知道还有什么厉害装备。总之就是别乱解锁。

I enjoyed the core of this game quite a bit. While I feel it needs some tweaking here and there it is a well executed game. In general, I would absolutely recommend this game for people that enjoy action combat. PROS -Great atmosphere with a lot of minor details - Nice addition of some extra game options to tailor the visual experience - Overall combat is engaging and so far seems to be fair with its challenges - Great visual design and nice enemy variety - Gear variety is great - Love the Gatorade cooler style method of refilling the healing flask. CONS - Parrying in this game has a very very short window and overall feels awkward. I'd argue this method of a parry mechanic in general is just not a positive design choice in any game that's used it. - The slow-mo when rolling from an attack makes the combat flow feel awkward - Having to spend every cent at the merchant before progressing feels quite bizarre of a design choice and pigeon holes the player a bit. Maybe have some sort of trade off for carrying a bunch of gold. Like punish me for my greed or something. Nitpicks/Minor suggestions - Give me an option to remove the HUD display for the controls on the right-hand side. - When switching gear the stat text on the new item will be green even when the stat is the same. It'd be cool if it was yellow just to give a bit more of the color communication to indicate it is an equal trade in the stat. Super minor nitpick though. - The CRT filter makes the screen quite blue which diminishes the gritty feel of the graphics. CRTs do not make the screen blue, still I'd like to praise the developer for its addition. Maybe just a slight reduction in the blue would help. - Please let me be able to sprint while locked on. Not being able to feels quite clunky and reminds me of my Dark Souls 2 woes. - Not sure if intentional but I can change the direction of my roll mid-roll. This can have the effect of accidentally removing any distance gained from rolling. - Stealth would also be neato and diversify gameplay. - This could benefit from some sort of poise/stance system. Lets the player utilize aggression if they are aware of the enemies weaknesses. And also gives armor a stronger presence than just having passive defensive additions.

[quote] 《Tyrant's Realm》是由[url=https://store.steampowered.com/publisher/skystone]Skystone Games[/url]发行的一款有点魂味道的肉鸽游戏。玩家扮演一位奋起反抗的囚犯，一路过关斩将最终推翻暴君的统治，游戏画风比较怀旧复古，如果你觉得游戏还不够复古的话，还可以在设置中打开像素画风，感受复古“马赛克”世界。 游戏关卡设定为小关连接Boss关卡，每个关卡之间都会提供整顿区（商店解锁物品、恢复状态以及血瓶），每种关卡的风格都有所不一样，前面基础关卡敌人还各具特色，但是到后面关卡基本就是大杂烩，许多敌人重复出现，不过关底Boss都是有自己的特色机制。 https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3410311712 在小关探索主要是获取游戏币和装备图纸，游戏币用于在整顿区解锁装备，只有解锁的装备才会在后续反复游玩时有机会爆出来。游戏币可以通过破坏木桶、击败敌人获取，可以借助一些装备额外获取，例如有的衣服可以增加死亡掉落游戏币。游戏装备有三个类别，分别为红、绿以及黄，在小关探索时还会找到紫色的祭坛，祭坛可以选择强化类别，建议选择身上同色类别进行强化增益。 https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3410311738 本作的武器、装备也是很丰富，除了常见的刀剑系武器以外，还有指虎、拳套、镰刀以及锤等等，基本上是攻速越快的武器都是伤害低耐力消耗低，而攻速慢的那种武器耐力消耗高伤害高适合不贪刀偷刀，而护甲也是各式各样，什么轻甲赋毒、重装防御兵都可以在这里找到。 本作的战斗玩法比较简单，角色只有轻重攻击、翻滚和盾牌防御，大部分操作都会消耗耐力，盾牌在恰当时机释放还可以释放盾反，不过想要处决的话必须要把黄色处决条打满才能处决，盾反时机还是蛮宽裕的，比较吃玩家对敌人的招式熟悉程度。游戏总共关卡不算多，通关初始难度之后又会回到初始地解锁更高的难度供玩家继续挑战， https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3410311640 游戏价格比较合适，并且目前也有首发折扣促销，推荐喜欢怀旧肉鸽游戏的玩家来尝试本作~ [quote] 游玩百态，将游玩心得用汉语化作玩家的指明灯，(๑•̀ㅂ•́)و✧ [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35402408/]点击这里关注汉化语录~[/url] 如果喜欢这个评测，请点个赞让更多人看见 [/quote] [/quote]

I usually never review a game before beating it, but Tyrant's Realm is not a game I feel that I'd have to beat to point out its flaws. Let me start by saying that this game isn't bad. But it's not very good either. This really is one of those cases where a "so-so" button would be appropriate. So many of the reviews on the front page are positive. But while a handful of the reviews note this game's jank and glaring flaws (despite recommending the game), many of them show less than 2 hours of playtime, with them singing its praises as another addition to the souls-like genre. Now, I'm no grand expert in souls-like games, but I can tell you that, without a doubt, Tyrant's Realm is [b]not[/b] a souls-like. It's ties or grasp on anything souls-related is superficial at worst and surface level paint at best. More accurately, this is a scuffed 3D Dead Cells, touting (optional) PS1-era visuals. Most of its core mechanics are clearly inspired by DC, albeit heavily diluted in nature. For instance, in DC, souls is a currency which can be used at hubs in-between most levels to unlock weapons, skills, upgrades, and skins that you've found blueprints for. They're also used to increase the rarity of loot you find while exploring levels. Souls can be obtained from scrolls you collect and from bosses when you defeat them (as well as some random events). In Tyrant's realm, coins are similar to DC's souls, yet coins can only be reliably and consistently obtained from killing bosses. Regular enemies drop coins too, but very rarely. Coins can also drop from breaking barrels (even at a more frequent rate than killing regular enemies). There are items like an armor that lets you loot coins from dead enemy but it's utility isn't enough to warrant keeping it over any other set of armor with likely better stats (or rather, it [i]shouldn't[/i] warrant it, but I'll come back to that a bit later). So if you want to actually be able to fund any of the blueprints or upgrades you find at the merchant, you'll have to run around breaking every barrel you find, just to max out as many coins as possible each level. And even though coins are similar to souls, the methods to obtain souls present more than enough opportunities for players to miss some sources and not feel like they need to grind levels for new gear unlocks. You even get rewarded souls for doing things like completing levels in a certain amount of time or taking no damage. So even if you run past all the possible chances to obtain souls in a level, Dead Cells sees that as a valid alternative to fighting every enemy or exploring every path. As a sort of add to that, one of those methods to obtain souls in DC, Scrolls, comes with passive stat boosts which affect your overall build and, particularly, gear that corresponds to the scroll's color. Well, Tyrant's Realm does something similar with skull altars you can find in a level that also have stats linked to the color of your gear (red, green, and yellow). But you only have two options at any altar, so one of the two options could be red and you have no red gear. DC's answer to this is that you can still choose a red scroll with zero red items in your build because the colors also represent hard stats like defense, power, and dexterity. In Tyrant's realm? If you have no gear of the selected color, it does nothing for you. Not actively, and not passively. It's just a waste of a potential stat increase. Speaking of your gear, you've got 3 categories: armors, weapons, and shields. Armors have the most going for them in terms of build potential, as most armors have skills tied to them, so choosing the right armor could affect how well your run goes. Oooor it would, [b]IF[/b] it wasn't all invalidated by two major factors: dodging and enemy hit reactions. I'm sort of skipping ahead of myself, but just hang with me here. Dodge rolls in this game gives you an [b]unreasonable[/b] amount of i-frames. There is zero reason to block an attack unless you're literally stuck and cannot move [b](yes, I have had that happen once against one of the bosses where I got cornered in-between the boss and the geometry of the his arena)[/b]. Dodging also slows down time each and every time you evade an attack, and when I say that the window for this invincible slowdown dodge is whale-schlong massive, I am [b]not[/b] joking. You can dodge roll towards an enemy almost a whole 2 seconds before their attack even starts and still avoid it. There are times where I would just be constantly rolling towards bosses (with an item that made dodge rolling and sprinting stamina-free mind you, which is insane not to take should you find it) just so I could negate their attacks completely and attacks with impunity while they recovered. Now the next factor may sound somewhat contrary to that last one but [b]enemies are completely unfazed by your attacks[/b]. Even basic enemies will no sell you wailing on them. This means that it's [b]ALWAYS[/b] the enemy's turn in any fight (outside of an extremely small handful of skills on some armors that uninterruptible). It also means that you can't reliably damage enemies without either taking damage or waiting for them to finish their attack every time they throw one out, and that you have to cheese their attacks with i-frame through dodging if you want to walk away from a fight intact. Couple that with the fact that locking onto an enemy disables the ability to sprint (yep, you read that right. You cannot sprint when locked onto an enemy) and this ultimately devolves the combat into never using any weapon that swings slower than a basic sword or a knife. Regardless of the damage output, you'll almost [b]never[/b] use a heavy weapon because the payoff in damage is not enough to ignore the fact that enemies just brush off your attack while you eat theirs and, possibly, get stunlocked from their combo or multiple enemies attacking you at once. It's a very arbitrary way to add difficulty which results in extremely rudimentary combat. Faster, often smaller weapon are way more reliable, use less stamina, and allow you to recover quicker should you need to dodge mid combo. There is almost zero reason to be concerned with defense from armors and shields (the defense stats as well) because of this. Your best, most consistent defensive tool is to just roll around like sonic the hedgehog and never get hit. Every boss I fought, I defeated with ease by abusing i-frames and attacking 2-3 times. Rinse and repeat. I [b]never[/b] needed to heal. I [b]never[/b] needed to block. I [b]never[/b] needed to worry. There are plenty of other things I could talk about like riposte attacks being tied to a meter meaning you can only do them every so often (Which don't offer anything to you. You [b]MAY[/b] get coins from a riposte kill, but that's because enemies randomly give coins, not from the attack itself), or that your character puts there shield on their back when not actively blocking, so you have to watch them draw their shield every time you want to block an attack (and you may still get hit. Again, it's useless. Just dodge.) but I think I've said enough. Far more than I should have really but I don't like leaving reviews without explanations of my experience. Again, this game isn't bad, not by a long shot; it's a solid [b]6/10[/b]. But I wouldn't recommend this game if you think you're getting a souls-like. You're not. You're getting a less-complex version of Dead Cells in the visual packaging of a less engaging Souls-like with (optional) PS1 visuals, which, if you're interested in either Dead Cells or Dark souls and have never played either, you should probably just play those game. They're far more engaging and far more rewarding to play, imo.

This game was a very frustrating experience. Its like they said "hey you know the PS1 games that were always so frustrating and anxiety inducing in your childhood? Lets make that!" There only seem to be 1-2 noise animations for each thing (enemy, item ect) so if you have the music turned down it really shows how sparse and few noises are in the game. Some items appear to be wrongly listed as one of the spears i picked up had a faster attack speed listed than the starter weapon but the animation is slower both on the heavy and fast attack. Blocking and parrying are very frustrating as some enemy attacks are easy to predict and prepare for and others have like a 3 second wind up but you don't know what one it is until the 2 second mark as it seems to be the same or very simlar animation. There is this odd skull meter in game that is never explained and is just full and flashing the entire time. Maybe there is something you can do with it but the tutorial didn't list anything. Damaging enemies can sometimes stun them. The issue is that you just never know when they get stunned. The normal fight will be something like "swing-roll/block enemy attack/attack combo-swing-block/roll enemy attack/attack combo" so taking advantage of any openings is just a frustrating experience. You CANNOT cancel an action when set in motion. If you wind up for a heavy attack you cannot cancel it to block or roll. To block there is this odd like 1/10th second delay on when you press the button and when the block happens. This makes it even harder to make a parry. Forgot to add, breaking barrels and such, sometimes when you swing at them they break and other times they just don't even when your weapon goes through the item or your character rolls against it. You just kind of roll up into it and nothing happens. Again its just many minor things about the game that just make it frustrating to play. All in all I just would not recommend this game. I know there are people who like challenging games and such but this one is what they call "punishing". It's just designed to be aggrivating and frustrating to the player.

Game is an absolutely awesome combination of Dark Souls, Dead Cells, and Nightmare Creatures. Sorry, Syphon Filter, there's a new king. Awesome, awesome game.

I truly believe this game could be an all time great. The bones of it are fantastic: A near-perfect mix of Dead Cells roguelite progression and Dark Souls combat mechanics. The crunchy graphics are great, it feels good to move and swing a weapon. Defeating hard enemies feels like an accomplishment. There are so many issues holding it back though. There is a distinct lack of enemy variety; 95% of the enemies you face in every area is either thin dude with sword, or fat dude with hammer. There are some other enemy types (acrobatic scythe enemies, dogs, spear-wielding enemies) but they are very few and far between, and do not feel different enough in the way you deal with them. Another issue is with gaining coins. The game uses Dead Cells progression, where you gain blueprints and coins during levels, and between levels you spend coins on the blueprints. But, you seem to obtain very few coins compared to the amount of blueprints you get. BUT! You have about a 33% chance of getting some extra coins when breaking barrels and other background objects. This means you will spend 60-70% of your time rolling into objects just to gain a couple more coins. I would rather there be NO coins/weapons in objects, and have a different way of obtaining them. Another issue for me is the armor. Each piece of armor has a special effect, but in my playthroughs it didn't feel like the effects were big enough to impact the game noticeably. The result is picking the armor with the best defensive stat (almost always the chunky yellow-color armor). This creates another issue, where you know you want the objective best armor, and want it as upgraded as possible. So you spend your "leveling" on the yellow-color level-ups (again like Dead Cells). Now, all the yellow items (weapons and shields) are better than every other color item. It seems to railroad you into the same build every time if you want the best result, which impacts replayability. And the lack of replayability is the worst. To me, the best parts of a roguelite are going back to the start, mixing and matching gear/upgrades for new ways to play (Think Binding of Isaac with the billions of different runs you can end up with). But there's only slashing weapons. Sure, they have different animations, but you're still swinging/jabbing a pointy thing at a humanoid with another pointy thing for the entire game. I beat the game after around 2 hours, was told a new difficulty is available, and was excited to play again with "elite" enemies... These are not new enemies, they are the exact same humanoids with pointy objects but now with red accents. and they do more damage. and have more health. so you fight them in the same way it just takes longer. ugh. Again, I truly feel in my soul that this could be an all-time great game. Dungeon-crawling is fantastic when paired with Dark Souls combat. Battles feel fluid and rewarding when the game gets more difficult. The maps are varied enough to not feel too same-y. So I BEG of the devs, please add more enemies. Add more incentive to make my run feel different than last time. Don't incentivize me to roll through every single barrel on the level to progress fast.

Hello Im Skill Incarnate and Welcome to My Games Review Series. My reviews cover indie games that i have bought, had gifted to me and have been provided by developers for review. In this episode I check out a brand new minimalist Soulslike called Tyrants Realm. This game is the breakout title from Team Tyrant, and is published by Skystone Games, who also released the masterful zombie survival game Undying. The game takes inspiration from Classic PS1 Era Games creating a soulslike, with a minimalist look and feel. Tyrants Realm follows an unknown prisoner who has broken free in order to hunt down the Tyrant, a evil wizard with the ability to manipulate reality. With nothing but a few simple weapons and your determination to succeed, youll battle your way through six unique zones, including an egyptian tomb, a snow covered fortress, a mine overrun with the undead and finally the Tyrants Realm, a gigantic castle where youll face off against the Tyrant in a final duel. With each failure youll get one step closer to freedom, unlocking powerful new weapons, armour and perks to aid in your next attempt. While the game is a little on the short side, the game features a roguelike progression system boasting over a hundred weapons and items to unlock as well as three separate difficulty levels to conquer. If your a soulslike enthusiast like myself, or your looking for games from the PlayStation 1 Era, then you should absolutely check out Tyrant Realm. Best of all, the game is a bargain at only $12 Please note: All opinions in this video are my own. I tried to play [b] Demon's Souls [/b] back in the day because I was incredibly drawn to the gritty setting and action combat. I dropped it VERY soon into playing it, cried uncle, and swore off [b] FromSoftware. [/b] Some years later when I endured a months-long recovery after a partially failed surgery, one of the things that brought me great relief was having a friend come over and play [b] Dark Souls [/b] while I watched curled up in the fetal position on the couch. I just never stopped being drawn to these games even though I am pitiful at playing them and have still not picked one up since that initial experience. I am impatient and greedy so I fail and become angry and frustrated before having any kind of fun. I saw [b] Splattercat [/b] reviewing [b] Tyrant's Realm [/b] and couldn't resist the price and throwback vibes. Right away I began having the same experience as I had with [b] Demon's Souls [/b] but this time I stuck with it and tried to [i] CALM DOWN. [/i] I am still within a sliver of health of beating the final boss but I am so so happy to say that it has completely brought me back around to seeing a new way to approach these kinds of games. Yes - this game is a souls-like for toddlers, I mean, comparatively speaking and all respect. I imagine a skilled player could easily sweep through the entire game within a couple hours. There are a handful of stages (like, seven?) with a boss at the end. You go through the main chunk of each stage fighting lower-level enemies, picking up health bar bumps and different gear, and then resting / spending gold for meta-progression / refilling health flasks at the Merchant's Tavern, then going into the boss fight. It is extremely generous. It is a very small project by a very small team and it is clearly a middle school love letter to [b] FromSoftware [/b] and a bygone era of low-res PS1 graphics. No, there is not a huge variety of anything here. But what it does, it does well. The controls are responsive, the weapons feel different and require adjustments to play style, and it is incredibly satisfying to pull off a perfect roll or parry. It's been wonderful and I am truly smitten with it as a title that has given me the cajones to once again try a souls game. This plays great on Steam Deck and I've only run into one issue where I was using my xbox controller, then put the Deck into sleep mode, and when I started it back up NOT using the xbox controller, the game would not respond to any inputs. I closed it and reopened it with still no response. I had to restart the Steam Deck entirely and only then would it respond. I was worried I would lose my progress but it saved almost right where I left off so no big deal. Coincidentally, the entire [b] Dark Souls [/b] series is on sale so I picked up the first one ready to jump in when I get an honest win in [b] Tyrant's Realm. [/b] I feel super satisfied about my progress, however slow, however clumsy, and would like to thank [b] Team Tyrant [/b] for what they've done here. Very fun! [b] 4 out of 5 [/b] for me.

很好玩的魂类游戏，结合了Rogue。动作手感很像黑暗之魂1。 画面虽然是复古像素风，但氛围营造得不错，很有沉浸感。 中文属于机翻，但是由于文本简单，所以玩起来没问题。 对于魂类游戏爱好者来说，是一盘美味的小吃。 武器我推荐用双手武器，攻击距离较长，打怪方便。 双手武器同样可以持盾，举起盾时会单持武器，在攻击时自动切换成双手持武器。 死亡惩罚较重，死后会掉落所有金钱和装备，在牢房重生，属于Rogue游戏里的典型。 所以，千万不要莽，不要贪刀，一切以存活为首要目的。先苟住再杀敌。 最后说一句，游戏体量很小。不到10小时，我就通关3周目，把最高难度给通了，看到了真结局。

连操作都是仿魂系的rogue小游戏，局外升级系统和死亡细胞一摸一样，连回冲血瓶的动作都一样就离谱。 个人感觉不是很好玩，怪物其实如果你稳定出后手没有一只怪有难度，BOSS难度都来自于神经刀和离谱的攻击范围，直接按住防御先花1分钟把BOSS攻击看完再打。 锁定敌人的功能不知道谁设计的，锁了不如不锁。你的人物在锁定的时候会直接挡住怪物的动作，设置也不能调锁定视角的角度，武器也没有什么特色。也没有魂系的韧性系统，全是韧狗，唯一不是韧狗的是这游戏的狗。

快跑，别玩，只值十块。把现在的完成度翻五倍上去才是个正常小品肉鸽游戏的内容量。 房间没变化小怪没变化战斗体验没变化他肉鸽了个寂寞。 解锁数值要求非常肝，解锁的东西也基本不能给游戏带来体验的变化，有变化，一点点。 锁定后任何攻击都会导致镜头晃，很难受。 小怪不足十种，每关一两种，然后后期大杂烩，纯纯狗屎。 怪全是韧狗。 boss充其量只能说有点设计，打起来也是一坨。 bd不起来，武器差别不大，凑红绿蓝给你点面板加成而已。

I like the concept, I was actually developing a similar idea for a game, but I was trying to combine Sekiro style combat with Slay the Spire decision making mechanics. Scope was too big for to solo. I've very sympathetic to the genre though, so I have to give this a thumbs up. I beat it on my first run, being very familiar with the genre, and it does seem to have some additional difficulty settings. Things I have to give props for: - Some unique ideas in the boss encounters - Really faithful to DS1 mechanics, albeit no charged heavy attack - Love the PS1 graphics Things that can use a bit of improvement: - More enemy variety - Enemies can also be a bit more thematic to the biomes they're in - I like the level up mechanic but have no idea what's going on with the different categories (greed, rage, something else) I don't know if this was a solo developer, but overall it's a really solid, well rounded, well made package. I encountered no bugs and everything worked as expected.

Things I liked: * The ps1-inspired graphics are nostalgic and pretty low demand, without looking bad. * I like the different themes of the environments, even if they are fairly predictable. * Runs don't take too long. Things I'm meh on: * All of the bosses except the first one have some unique gimmick or mechanic that makes them a little more than you might expect. However, after you fight them once, the surprise is gone and it becomes a chore to fight them again. Things I disliked: * The game lacks so much content. It only has about 8 enemies not counting bosses, the rooms across areas are largely the same with a different coat of paint, and many weapons share the same moveset and only differ a bit in reach, speed, damage. After a few runs, you'll have seen everything the game basically has. * The combat is extremely simple. Your moveset is like Dark Souls if you stripped away any of the complexity around damage types, status effects, roll speed based on equip weight, etc. This wouldn't be so bad, except enemies are also exceedingly simple; each one only has 2-4 moves, and they are all pretty well telegraphed. This combined with extremely simple map design where there's very little environmental danger, and it feels like a paint-by-number version of a FromSoft masterpiece painting. * There are about 8 different environments, and they have some surface differences, but are largely just squares connected to each other with each room containing one or two enemies. there's rarely any verticality and rooms are simple. There's only one map type with any secrets, there is only one npc (the merchant) with no lines, and the areas, enemies, and random objects in them, are all very basic and predictable. * The level up system and gear unlock system is taken directly from Dead Cells, with basically no alterations. I think this would have been more forgivable if the rest of the game had more to it to distract from it, or if the developer added their own unique twist. But that hasn't happened. * There are 3 difficulty levels. The first one is far too easy, the second is probably about right, and the 3rd sounds like an absolute chore. I think the core idea here is attractive; I really do want a great souls-like rogue-like experience. But this game lacks so much of what makes those games great: - The combination of tight combat and complexity of systems layered on top (status effects, damage types, weapon durability, buffs, equipment weight, single-hand vs two-hand vs dual wield, ranged options, items, spells, etc.) - interesting, unexpected environments to get lost in and fight in - weirdness...especially with bosses and enemies, but also just in general. What's great about fromsoft games is they always have some npcs, enemies, interactions, etc. that are just flat out strange. It makes them more memorable. This game's just so...basic. There's good bones here, but it's a glass of water that's trying to convince you it's a lake. It just needs more everything.

Team Tyrant, you're so close to a great game here. I was having a great time at first, I was into the style of this game and the concept was appealing though there are thousands upon thousands of Souls-likes out there. I swam through the first section pretty easily with only a few deaths as I learned the play style... I got past the first boss fight and the game got extremely difficult. I don't know if it's meant to do so but for some reason after beating that character relatively easily the difficulty curve shot up so high it doesn't feel like I can progress. There feels like a false difficulty by lack of items or upgrades but stronger and multiplied enemies. I feel like I shouldn't be dying on the first rooms that have enemies after dying already before that because my character couldn't "grow". I know; "skill issue" but I apparently am not the only one having a bad feeling about the stats and animation timing/balancing. Doesn't seem to matter what items or layout is present. Blocking and parries feel almost like you shouldn't bother because they work less often than they perform well. Dodging can work, but it's also unreliable for the most part. Enemies can swarm you from rooms you haven't even looked into yet and this can happen before you have any item that would give you a remote fighting chance against two enemies, let alone 3-4. It just got stressful and frustrating. With some tweaks it could be really solid overall! To leave off with a positive or two, I love the visuals. The Garrett (From the Thief Trilogy) homage was really neat to see. Could be a great gem but it's not quite there. Make it work and I'll gladly change or rescind my negative vote. Tl;Dr to those who can't read paragraphs: I suppose I can simplify it into the balance feels off and never recovers or feels quite right after multiple runs. Doesn't matter the randomly given items or upgrades. I hope Team Tyrant realize they have a decent start to what they've made. Just needs some tweaks and patching.

Look, I really enjoyed this game. It was a lot of fun, scratched the roguelike itch, and I've sunk many more hours than I expected into this going "just one more run". However it's janky af, with certain bugs being completely run-ruining. And that's kind of disrespectful. There's nothing more annoying than playing a game like this (especially on a time-trial or something) than falling through the floor and having to reload the level, only to find that every single enemy has also fallen through the floor, along with the enemy that holds the key to the next level. The mouse controls seem to constantly get stuck for no reason despite fiddling with the options, which is totally weird for a low-spec game that could be practically run on a potato - but A quick google search tells me that these are not issues independent to me or my reasonable PC setup. Rather than choosing to fix these issues on an otherwise completely entertaining game, instead the devs have turned their focus to making DLC - which is great, but first: fix the bugs on your base game first.

[b]Great pocket action rogue-like with souls-like elements. Tyrant's Realm is focused on pure fun gameplay and mostly nothing else, which is absolutely not a bad thing.[/b] You run, kill, pick/swap items from chests/barrels, go to the next room, upgrade items/stats at altars, kill more, rinse & repeat a few times, and after several rooms you might make it to the Merchant's Lounge. There, you refill your health flask and buy/unlock items (which are then available in the item pool, also in subsequent runs), flask upgrades, and hidden passages. From the Merchant's Lounge, you can advance either to a boss room or to the next biome (after defeating the current biome's boss), until finally encountering the titular Tyrant. If (when) you die, you start over from the first biome with default equipment (unless you bought perks for random starting gear from the item pool) and as many flask uses as times you upgraded it (or default 3). Combat mostly resembles the first 2 parts of Dark Souls, so it might not fit players who prefer more fast-paced titles. Even though it lacks anything beyond light/heavy melee attacks + armor's special (if available), block/parry, and dodge, I found it really satisfying nevertheless. For a game that's priced at 5$, it offers quite a lot when it comes to replayability, especially if you hunt for all the achievements. That's an easy recommendation from me.
